paragraphs.en: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009. For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least. “Hooray! At last!” wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided classical-music critic.
paragraphs.zh: 自2009年突然宣布任命以来，纽约爱乐乐团聘请艾伦·吉尔伯特担任下一任音乐总监的决定，就一直是古典音乐界热议的话题。至少可以说，大部分反应是正面的。一贯严肃的古典音乐评论家安东尼·托马西尼写道：“好极了！终于等到了！”

paragraphs.en: One of the reasons why the appointment came as such a surprise, however, is that Gilbert is comparatively little known. Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert’s appointment in the Times, calls him “an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him.” As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这项任命之所以令人如此惊讶，原因之一在于吉尔伯特相对鲜为人知。就连曾在《纽约时报》上主张任命吉尔伯特的托马西尼，也称他是“一位朴实无华的音乐家，丝毫没有那种令人敬畏的大指挥家的派头”。对于一支历来由古斯塔夫·马勒和皮埃尔·布列兹等音乐大师执掌的乐团来说，这样评价其下一任音乐总监，很可能至少会让《纽约时报》的部分读者觉得，称赞的分量实在不够。

paragraphs.en: For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one. To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting orchestral music. All I have to do is to go to my CD shelf, or boot up my computer and download still more recorded music from iTunes.
paragraphs.zh: 就我而言，我不知道吉尔伯特是不是一位伟大的指挥家，甚至不知道他是不是一位优秀的指挥家。诚然，他演奏的有趣作品种类繁多，令人印象深刻，但为了聆听有趣的管弦乐，我没必要去艾弗里·费舍尔音乐厅，也没必要去任何其他地方。我只需走到自己的唱片架前，或打开电脑，从iTunes下载更多录制好的音乐就行了。

paragraphs.en: Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point. For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century. These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often much higher in artistic quality than today’s live performances; moreover, they can be “consumed” at a time and place of the listener’s choosing. The widespread availability of such recordings has thus brought about a crisis in the institution of the traditional classical concert.
paragraphs.zh: 那些热衷音乐会的人若回应说，录音无法代替现场演奏，那就是没有抓住问题的要点。为了争取热爱艺术的公众的时间、注意力和金钱，古典音乐演奏家不仅必须与歌剧院、舞蹈团、剧团和博物馆竞争，还必须与二十世纪古典音乐大师的演出录音竞争。这些录音价格便宜，随处可得，而且在艺术质量上往往远高于当今的现场演出；此外，听众可以自行选择时间和地点来“消费”它们。因此，这类录音的广泛普及，已经给传统古典音乐会这一制度带来了危机。

paragraphs.en: One possible response is for classical performers to program attractive new music that is not yet available on record. Gilbert’s own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into “a markedly different, more vibrant organization.” But what will be the nature of that difference? Merely expanding the orchestra’s repertoire will not be enough. If Gilbert and the Philharmonic are to succeed, they must first change the relationship between America’s oldest orchestra and the new audience it hopes to attract.
paragraphs.zh: 一种可能的应对办法，是让古典音乐演奏家安排演出尚未有录音发行、又富有吸引力的新音乐。吉尔伯特本人对新音乐的兴趣，已受到广泛关注。古典音乐评论家亚历克斯·罗斯称，他有能力把纽约爱乐乐团变成“一个明显不同、更有活力的机构”。但这种不同究竟应体现在哪里呢？仅仅扩充乐团的曲目是不够的。如果吉尔伯特和纽约爱乐乐团想要取得成功，就必须首先改变这支美国历史最悠久的乐团与它希望吸引的新听众之间的关系。
